title: Remotes, Fetch, Pull & Push Collaboration
description: Connect local repositories to remote hosts like GitHub, understand remote-tracking branches, and synchronize changes with fetch, pull, and push.

blocks.content:
## What is a Remote?

A remote repository is a version of your project hosted on a network or the Internet (such as GitHub, GitLab, or Bitbucket). A remote is simply a bookmark or alias pointing to a repository URL.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    DevA[("Local Repo A")] <-->|"push / pull"| Origin[("Remote: origin\n(e.g., GitHub)")]
    Origin <-->|"push / pull"| DevB[("Local Repo B")]
```

When you clone a repository, Git automatically names that remote repository `origin`.

## Managing Remote Connections

```bash
# List configured remotes with URLs
git remote -v
# Output:
# origin  https://github.com/user/repo.git (fetch)
# origin  https://github.com/user/repo.git (push)

# Add a new remote alias
git remote add origin https://github.com/user/repo.git

# Rename an existing remote
git remote rename origin upstream

# Remove a remote
git remote remove upstream
```

## `git fetch` vs `git pull`

The difference between fetching and pulling is one of the most important concepts in collaborative Git:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    Remote[("Remote Repository (origin/main)")] -->|"git fetch"| Tracking[("Remote Tracking Branch (origin/main in local .git)")]
    Tracking -->|"git merge / rebase"| Local[("Local Branch (main)")]
    Remote -->|"git pull (fetch + merge)"| Local
```

1. **`git fetch`**: Safely downloads all commits, files, and refs from the remote without modifying your working files or moving your local branch pointers. It only updates `origin/<branch>`.
2. **`git pull`**: Runs `git fetch` and immediately attempts to merge (or rebase) the downloaded commits into your currently checked-out branch.

## Pushing Changes to Remotes

To share your local commits with teammates:

```bash
# Push the current branch and set up upstream tracking (-u)
git push -u origin feature-auth

# Subsequent pushes on this branch require only:
git push

# Delete a remote branch
git push origin --delete feature-auth
```

The `-u` (or `--set-upstream`) flag links your local branch directly to `origin/feature-auth`, enabling short-hand `git push` and `git pull` without specifying remote and branch names every time.

blocks.question: What is the primary difference between 'git fetch' and 'git pull'?
options: git fetch only downloads data to remote-tracking branches without altering your working tree; git pull fetches and merges into your active branch
git pull is for cloning repositories; git fetch is for creating new commits
git fetch requires root permissions, while git pull does not
git pull only checks network connectivity without downloading commits
blocks.explanation: 'git fetch' downloads remote changes safely without touching your working tree or current branch. 'git pull' fetches and then automatically merges changes into your current branch.

blocks.question: What does the '-u' flag in 'git push -u origin main' accomplish?
options: It forces an overwrite of the remote branch even if history diverges
It establishes an upstream tracking link between the local branch and origin/main
It uninstalls untracked files from the remote server
It encrypts the payload before sending
blocks.explanation: The '-u' (--set-upstream) flag creates a tracking relationship so future 'git push' and 'git pull' commands default to that remote branch.
